2. Learn how it makes its sound, one idea at a time.

## What it is

- The **Wurlitzer 200** came out in **1968**; it was the most popular Wurlitzer, about 88,000 built (Wikipedia, "Wurlitzer electronic piano").
- The **200A** came in **1974** and was made until 1983, with a better shield against mains hum (Wikipedia).
- Most Wurlitzers have **64 keys**. The 200 weighs 56 pounds without legs, with a 30-watt amplifier and two speakers facing the player (Wikipedia).

## Its sound

- The sound is made "by striking a metal reed with a felt hammer" (Wikipedia).
- The reed moves near an **electrostatic pickup** held at 170 V DC; its motion changes the charge and makes the signal (Wikipedia).
- The pickup is not even on both sides of the reed, so hard notes gain **even harmonics** and the amp pushes them further: the Wurli's reedy growl (this page's model).
- Its vibrato knob is really a **tremolo** at one speed: only the depth changes (Wikipedia: "Vibrato (single speed)").

## The panel

The Wurlitzer's panel drawn after the real one (not a copy; no logos). Turn the knobs, flip the switches, play the keys below it,
the computer keys or a MIDI keyboard. **Simple** shows every control as a slider, including the adjustments inside the instrument.
The sound is this site's own physical model (see [how it is modelled](epiano-compare.qmd#how-each-one-is-modelled)); nobody has
compared it with the real instrument. Facts come from the Wikipedia articles listed under Works Cited (read 2026-11-26). The service manuals were not read for these pages, so control legends and places that Wikipedia does not give are marked unverified.

## A guided tour

<div class="ik-step" data-set="{&quot;model&quot;:&quot;wurli&quot;}" data-riff="soul">

**The plain 200A.** Volume 7, Vibrato 0. Listen: thinner and reedier than a Rhodes.

</div>

<div class="ik-step" data-set="{&quot;model&quot;:&quot;wurli&quot;,&quot;gap&quot;:9,&quot;drive&quot;:6}" data-riff="soft_hard">

**Reed close to the pickup, amp driven.** Soft to hard: listen for the growl on the hard hits.

</div>

<div class="ik-step" data-set="{&quot;model&quot;:&quot;wurli&quot;,&quot;vib&quot;:7}" data-riff="soul">

**Vibrato 7.** The level goes up and down at one speed: a tremolo.

</div>

<div class="ik-step" data-set="{&quot;model&quot;:&quot;wurli&quot;,&quot;tone&quot;:2,&quot;drive&quot;:1}" data-riff="soul">

**A dark, clean Wurli.** Speaker brightness 2 and little drive: closer to a soft ballad sound.

</div>

## Famous tracks

Each video was checked on YouTube (oEmbed, 2026-11-26). Listen first, then press **▶** for a starting setting on the panel above.

### "The Logical Song" (Supertramp)

[▶ The Logical Song](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=low6Coqrw9Y) on YouTube (Supertramp - Topic).

Wikipedia names Supertramp's Wurlitzer on it. Bouncy, bright chords with a little bite.

<div class="ik-step" data-set="{&quot;model&quot;:&quot;wurli&quot;,&quot;gap&quot;:6,&quot;drive&quot;:5,&quot;tone&quot;:6}" data-riff="soul">

**Starting setting** (Wurlitzer): gap 6, drive 5, tone 6. Then change it until it sounds like the record to you.

</div>

### "Dreamer" (Supertramp)

[▶ Dreamer](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7fdAFmtq-o8) on YouTube (Supertramp - Topic).

Also named by Wikipedia. A fast repeated chord figure: hard hits that bark.

<div class="ik-step" data-set="{&quot;model&quot;:&quot;wurli&quot;,&quot;gap&quot;:8,&quot;drive&quot;:6,&quot;hard&quot;:7}" data-riff="soft_hard">

**Starting setting** (Wurlitzer): gap 8, drive 6, hard 7. Then change it until it sounds like the record to you.

</div>

### "You're My Best Friend" (Queen)

[▶ Queen - You&#x27;re My Best Friend (Official Video)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HaZpZQG2z10) on YouTube (Queen Official).

John Deacon played the Wurlitzer (Wikipedia). A steady comping part under the voices.

<div class="ik-step" data-set="{&quot;model&quot;:&quot;wurli&quot;,&quot;gap&quot;:5,&quot;drive&quot;:3}" data-riff="soul">

**Starting setting** (Wurlitzer): gap 5, drive 3. Then change it until it sounds like the record to you.

</div>

```{=html}
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>What does the Wurlitzer&#x27;s hammer hit?</b></p><ul><li>A metal reed</li><li>A tine</li><li>A string</li><li>A bell</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Wikipedia.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>What kind of pickup does it have?</b></p><ul><li>Electrostatic</li><li>Magnetic</li><li>Piezo</li><li>A microphone</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Wikipedia: 170 V DC electrostatic pickup.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>How many speeds has its vibrato?</b></p><ul><li>One</li><li>Two</li><li>Any</li><li>None: it has no vibrato</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Wikipedia: single speed.</p></div>

```
